title: Update pnpm to v12.21.0
body:
This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`12.20.0` → `12.21.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/12.20.0/12.21.0) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/12.21.0?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/12.21.0?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/12.20.0/12.21.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/12.20.0/12.21.0?slim=true) | --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.21.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.21.0): pnpm 12.21 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.20.0...v12.21.0) pnpm 12.21.0 lets `pnpm store add` prepare tarball and git dependencies for offline installs. It also makes repeated installs keep their peer dependency choices and fixes several `lockfile.format: v13`, `nodeLinker: hoisted`, and `pnpm deploy` failures. If a pnpr server refuses a setting, pnpm now resolves locally. ##### Minor Changes - `pnpm store add` run in a project now prepares downloaded tarballs for every lockfile entry that pins them. Besides registry packages, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` can then install dependencies on a tarball URL and dependencies on a git host such as GitHub whose lockfile entry records an `integrity`. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installs that failed - pnpm now reads a lockfile with a mapping key longer than 1,024 characters written as `'key':`, without the `? ` marker. Before, `pnpm install` and other commands failed on such a lockfile with `ERR_PNPM_BROKEN_LOCKFILE`. - With `lockfile.format: v13`, `pnpm install` no longer fails to create or rewrite the lockfile when a package declares many of its dependencies as peers. - Fixed `pnpm deploy` failing with `lockfile.format: v13` when injected workspace packages have hashed peer bindings. - Frozen installs with v13 lockfiles now accept valid peer dependencies of injected workspace packages that use catalogs. - Fixed injected workspace packages that depend on themselves linking to a nonexistent directory. - `pnpm install` with `frozenStore` enabled no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_STORE_NEEDS_BUILD` when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted`. `pnpm fetch` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` no longer populates global virtual store links or modifies linked agent skills, and it preserves an existing hoisted `node_modules` directory [#​18037](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18037). - A `requirements.txt` beside a `pyproject.toml` that declares `[tool.uv.workspace]` without a `[project]` table no longer makes that directory a Python project. `pnpm install` stopped there with an error when the directory had a `.venv` that pnpm did not create [#​18023](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18023). ##### Peer dependencies - Repeated installs no longer change the peer dependency providers that the previous install chose. This covers adding, updating, or removing a dependency, projects that use different ranges of one dependency, dependency cycles, and injected dependencies with `autoInstallPeers: false` [pnpm/tasks#221](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/221). An unchanged install keeps a valid locked peer provider even when a direct dependency provides another compatible version. Explicit `pnpm add` and `pnpm update` requests take precedence over it. - Workspace projects that select different versions of a peer provider no longer share one copy of the package that depends on it. This affected peers reached through an aliased dependency or a peer dependency cycle. - A removed dependency no longer comes back as a peer provider. Before, a direct dependency removed with `autoInstallPeers: false` could be restored from an old peer resolution, and a removed one could still supply its old peer context. - With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, `pnpm install` no longer creates duplicate copies of a package whose resolved peers are identical. A package also no longer loads a copy of its dependency that was resolved with different peer versions [#​18003](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18003). - `pnpm deploy` now binds optional peers declared only in `peerDependenciesMeta` for linked workspace packages. The deployed manifest and lockfile also retain these peers when filtering dependency groups. ##### Running scripts - Scripts now stop when pnpm's process group is killed while they are starting. - Bin shims in the global virtual store no longer include the hoisted modules directory of the project that installed them [#​18035](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18035). - `pnpm pipeline` now rebuilds local packages and reruns build scripts after it restores a shared Cargo build cache with Cargo 1.100 or newer. Before, a worktree could reuse build-script output from the worktree that created the cache. ##### pnpr - If the pnpr server refuses a setting the install uses, or cannot return the lockfile format pnpm reads, `pnpm install` and `pnpm update` print a warning and resolve locally. Cargo and Python resolution also fall back to resolving locally. pnpm now rejects a pnpr resolution of npm dependencies that does not name its lockfile format. - `pnpm install` with `pnprServer` now limits the size of the server's resolve and lockfile verification responses. An oversized response ends the request with an error. - pnpm now displays pnpr error codes and reasons when remote requests fail. ##### Other commands and settings - `pnpm setup` and the install script now support PowerShell as the login shell on Linux and macOS. They add `PNPM_HOME` to `PATH` in `profile.ps1` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/powershell` or `~/.config/powershell` [#​18026](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18026). - A `lockfileDir` setting that points at the default lockfile directory now installs the same way as leaving it unset [pnpm/tasks#275](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/275). #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors

title: Show the next unit in bytesToString when rounding reaches it
body:

## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue or discussion
  in the additional information section.
-->

`bytesToString` picked the unit before rounding, so a value just below a unit boundary rounded up to 1024 of the smaller unit, e.g. `1048575` bytes was shown as `1024 KB` instead of `1 MB`.

If rounding reaches 1024, the next unit is used.

title: Transliterate Cyrillic х as kh in slugify
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue or discussion
  in the additional information section.
-->

The Cyrillic `х` appeared in both the single-character map and the `complex_cyrillic` table. The single-character map runs first and replaced it with `h`, so the `kh` entry was never used, and e.g. `кухня` became `kuhnia` instead of `kukhnia`.

`х` is removed from the single-character map (with its counterpart in the replacement string), so it's now transliterated as `kh`, consistent with the other entries in `complex_cyrillic`.

Adds tests for Cyrillic transliteration.

title: Fix IP address validation for leading zeros and embedded IPv4
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue or discussion
  in the additional information section.
-->

Fixes two problems in the shared IP address patterns used by `isIPAddress`, `isIPv6Address` and the network config forms' `pattern` attribute.

**IPv4 octets with leading zeros** such as `010.1.1.1` were accepted. Core's `ipaddress` validation rejects them, and they're ambiguous (octal in some parsers). The octet pattern no longer allows leading zeros, including the IPv4 part of an IPv6 address.

**IPv6 addresses ending in dotted IPv4** after five or six groups were rejected, e.g. `1:2:3:4:5:6:1.2.3.4` and `1:2:3:4:5::1.2.3.4`. The pattern only listed a few of the embedded-IPv4 forms by hand.

The IPv6 pattern is now built from the RFC 3986 (section 3.2.2) grammar, where every form ends in either two groups or an IPv4 address, and it reuses the stricter IPv4 octet.

To check the rewrite, I compared it locally against Node's `net.isIPv4`/`net.isIPv6` on about 500k generated addresses: there were no mismatches. Compared with the old pattern, the only differences were the two fixes above. The patterns also still compile with the `v` flag that browsers use for `pattern` attributes.

Adds tests.
